jobs.title: Billing Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the role

Your job is to own billing at E2B — everything that touches how we charge customers, collect revenue, and capture the data behind it. The metering pipeline, the Stripe integration, invoicing, collections, and the billing surfaces developers see in the dashboard.

Your code will be responsible for collecting data metrics, creating and sending invoices and reconciliation of payments for our customers across the globe.

We have a billing system. Your job is to take it over end to end and redesign it. Engineering, finance, and customers all depend on the system and the data it produces, and you'll work across all three. When a customer asks why their invoice looks the way it does, you're the person who can answer. Responsibilities include:

  • Owning the services behind billing end-to-end — usage metering, charge calculation, invoicing, payments, and the data models underneath them

  • Owning the Stripe integration end-to-end: subscriptions, Billing Meters, and enterprise invoicing edge cases

  • Building billing automation: failed-payment recovery, collections, proration and plan changes, credits, refunds, and disputes

  • Working with engineers across Core, Platform, and Dashboard to get the data billing depends on, and defining the contracts for it

  • Partnering with finance on reconciliation, revenue reporting, and audit-readiness

  • Making architectural decisions around observability, testing, and security

What we're looking for

  • Understanding of metric collection, metered usage, Pay-as-you-go, billing cycles - being able to understand finance requirements and translate them into well tested code

  • Backend engineer with 5+ years billing systems experience, with deep expertise in Go

  • Strong API design — REST/RPC, contracts and versioning

  • Solid with PostgreSQL: schema design, query optimization, migrations, and reasoning about data at scale

  • Backend fundamentals: authentication/authorization, server-side performance, and building real-time data flows (WebSockets, SSE)

  • Experienced with charging logic, collections, billing automation, and billing-related data flows

  • Comfortable with complex invoicing, SKUs, usage-/contract-based billing, and third-party payment platforms

  • Strong cross-functional communication skills, especially with finance

  • Comfortable owning a system end-to-end with high autonomy

  • Able to work through ambiguity and figure things out independently

What it’s like to work at E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with in-person (4 days on-site, 1 day WFH) offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 9-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.

About the role

You'll run the Platform team that ships reliable work fast, and you'll co-own the entire platform: cloud operations, Terraform automation, BYOC, and on-call. You'll lead both the people and the quality of what they deliver, so that E2B's core infrastructure is fast, secure, and reliable at any scale, customers trust us with their agents' execution, and product teams ship on top of the platform without thinking about it.

Your job will be:

  • Leading a platform engineering team — 1:1s, performance reviews, career growth, hiring, and day-to-day people management

  • Owning delivery and quality — making sure work meets the definition of done before it ships, not just gets assigned

  • Running project management for the team — scoping work, leading projects, and delivering on time

  • Owning day-to-day job allocation, unblocking, and providing technical context and direction to the team

  • Owning technical guidance and code-review standards, and translating core architecture into how your team builds

  • Sitting in the technical leadership group — surfacing signal from projects, operations, and on-call up to leadership

  • Planning the on-call rota — keeping it staffed, published, and followed, and owning incident follow-up

  • Staying hands-on as a major contributor to projects yourself

  • Experience leading or mentoring a team of infrastructure or platform engineers, with the judgment to make calls and own outcomes

  • 5+ years building infrastructure, especially distributed systems, and operating it at scale

  • 5+ years of Linux fundamentals — kernel, networking, storage, namespaces, containers

  • Hands-on experience with cloud operations, Terraform/IaC, and orchestration technologies like Kubernetes or Nomad

  • A strong bar for delivery and quality — you ship reliable work fast and hold your team to the same standard

  • Excited to work in person on a DevTool product and comfortable working closely with users

  • Proactive, not afraid to take ownership of part of the product

About the role

As a Technical Recruiter at E2B, you’ll build the team that will define the future of the company. This is a early role where you’ll help shape our hiring philosophy, recruiting processes, and talent brand as we scale.

You’ll partner directly with the Head of Talent and leadership team to identify hiring needs, source, and close exceptional candidates. You’ll help establish E2B as a destination for top engineers, builders, and operators in the developer and AI ecosystem, while ensuring every hire raises the bar.

From designing interview processes to closing senior candidates, you’ll play a critical role in assembling a world-class team capable of executing E2B’s ambitious vision.

What we’re looking for

Experience:
At least 5+ years in recruiting or talent acquisition, ideally in high-growth startups or DevTool / AI companies. Experience hiring technical talent (especially engineers) is essential.

Startup mindset:
Comfortable operating in early-stage environments where speed, autonomy, and ownership matter. You enjoy building processes where none exist and iterating quickly.

Technical recruiting expertise:
Proven ability to source and close strong engineering candidates in competitive markets. You understand developer profiles, technical hiring signals, and how to engage top technical talent.

End-to-end ownership:
You can run the full recruiting lifecycle, from sourcing strategy and outreach to interview design, candidate experience, and closing.

Ability to partner with founders and leaders to define hiring plans, role scorecards, and structured hiring processes.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the role

You will be building the next cloud platform for running AI software - a cloud where AI apps are building other software apps.

Your job will be:

  1. Building a distributed system for millions and billions of AI agents running on E2B

  2. Building an orchestrator for placing sandboxes in the right nodes

  3. Adding support for sandbox live migrations

  4. Making sure our self-hosting DX is as smooth as possible (we’re open-source)

  5. Not letting our sandboxes take more than 200ms to start (starting with the user hitting enter)

  6. Scaling to millions and later billions of sandboxes running at the same time

  7. Building an observability stack starting at the kernel level of virtual machines

We’re looking for an infrastructure engineer passionate about making things run fast and efficiently, and running A LOT of them at the same time.

If you aren’t afraid of going into the kernel of a VM and words like Firecracker, eBPF, UFFD, block device, L4 load balancing, noisy neighbor problem, or hugepages sound exciting to you, we want to hear from you!

 

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years building distributed systems - You've operated infrastructure at serious scale (100K+ RPS, multi-region, PB-scale data) and understand the trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in practice, not just theory

  • Deep Linux internals expertise - You're comfortable working at the kernel level. You've debugged performance issues using eBPF, understand CPU scheduling, memory management, and can explain the difference between cgroups v1 and v2 without looking it up

  • VM hypervisor experience - You've worked with Firecracker, QEMU, KVM, or similar. You understand virtio, know what a hypercall is, and have opinions about nested virtualization trade-offs

  • Systems programming skills - Strong in at least one of: Go, Rust, C/C++. You've written performance-critical code and know when to reach for lock-free data structures, memory-mapped files, or io_uring

  • Production orchestration experience - You've built or operated orchestration systems (Kubernetes, Nomad, or custom). You understand bin-packing algorithms, resource scheduling, and have dealt with noisy neighbor problems at scale

  • Performance obsession - You've shaved milliseconds off hot paths, understand CPU caches and memory locality, and have profiled production systems under load. You know what "p99 latency" means and care deeply about making it better

  • Networking expertise - Strong understanding of L4/L7 load balancing, network namespaces, iptables/nftables, and how to build secure, isolated network topologies for multi-tenant systems

  • Excited about open source - Comfortable with our code and infrastructure being public. You contribute to discussions, write clear documentation, and help the community succeed with self-hosting

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with userfaultfd (UFFD), copy-on-write mechanisms, or lazy loading

  • GPU passthrough or PCIe device virtualization experience

  • Built or maintained infrastructure for AI/ML workloads

  • Contributions to Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, or similar open source projects

  • Experience with observability at scale (distributed tracing, kernel-level metrics)

What it’s like to work at E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with in-person (4 days on-site, 1 day WFH) offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 9-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.

jobs.title: Product Engineer - Backend Developer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the role

Your job will be to own and scale the backend that powers the E2B Dashboard and SDK — the APIs, data, and services developers rely on to run, monitor, and debug their sandboxes. You're the backend counterpart to our dashboard engineers: they own the experience, you own the services and data behind it, and together you ship product end-to-end.

This is product/application backend - APIs, data layer, auth, billing, usage metrics, real-time log/metric pipelines. It is not our low-level infrastructure (Firecracker, orchestration, the sandbox runtime) - that lives with our Core and Platform teams, who you'll integrate with but not duplicate.

The split is roughly 80% Go backend, 20% TypeScript — you live in Go, but you're comfortable dropping into the Next.js app to wire things up end-to-end and unblock the frontend rather than throwing work over a wall.

You'll build enterprise-grade services that scale to 100k+ weekly active users. Responsibilities include:

  • Owning the Go services behind the dashboard and SDK — APIs, data models, and the contracts the frontend builds on

  • Designing auth/authorization, billing, and usage-metering surfaces

  • Building the real-time backends (WebSockets, SSE) that feed sandbox logs and metrics to the dashboard

  • Optimizing data access and server-side performance — query design, caching, response times

  • Partnering closely with dashboard engineers to ship features end-to-end, and with Core/Platform on the boundaries where product meets infrastructure

  • Making architectural decisions around observability, testing, and security best practices

This role requires a high amount of ownership and the ability to take projects from 0 to 1. You'll have deep autonomy to make backend and product decisions. If you see a better way to build something, you build it.

What we're looking for

  • 3-5+ years shipping production backend services, with deep expertise in Go

  • Strong API design — REST/RPC, contracts, versioning, and an eye for the interface the frontend actually needs

  • Solid with PostgreSQL: schema design, query optimization, migrations, and reasoning about data at scale

  • Backend fundamentals: authentication/authorization, server-side performance, and building real-time data flows (WebSockets, SSE)

  • Working TypeScript(Next.js is a plus) competence — you won't live here, but you can move into the app-router frontend to wire up a feature end-to-end and not be lost

  • Understand data fetching patterns on frontend side

  • Excited to work in person from Prague on a devtool product

  • Ownership mentality: you see projects through from conception to launch to iteration

  • Comfortable talking to customers and explaining technical tradeoffs

  • Not being afraid to take ownership of your part of the product

  • Great communication, curiosity, and interest in the AI space

If you join E2B, you'll get a lot of freedom. We expect you to be proactive and take ownership. You'll be taking projects from 0 to 1 with the support of the rest of the team.

What it’s like to work at E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with in-person (4 days on-site, 1 day WFH) offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 9-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the role

E2B has started billions of Firecracker sandboxes across regions on Google Cloud, AWS and Azure. Every sandbox is a real virtual machine that has to start in well under a second, resume from a snapshot on a different host, and share a host with up to about 200 others without noticing them.

Your job will be to build and own the Go service on every host that creates, pauses, resumes and tears down sandboxes, along with the Linux underneath it: host networking, memory and isolation. You'll work closely with our sandbox team in Prague, who own the Firecracker runtime, the guest kernel, sandbox storage and live migration, and with our infrastructure engineers, who put the platform together.

We're hiring more than one engineer into this role, each with a different focus: some go deepest on Linux and how sandboxes run on the host, others on sandbox networking. Our runtime is open source at github.com/e2b-dev/runtime, and the sandbox package is a good place to see what you'd work on.

Responsibilities include:

  • Making sandboxes start fast and keeping them fast as the fleet grows to millions and later billions of sandboxes, with starts under 200ms

  • Evolving the architecture of the software that runs sandboxes on every host, so it can change without disrupting them

  • Making the sandbox lifecycle reliable under failure, so no sandbox is leaked or lost when a process or host dies

  • Keeping the host OS and kernel current across the fleet, rolling out upgrades without disrupting running sandboxes

  • Building the sandbox network: isolation, egress control and addressing for untrusted workloads

  • Enforcing resource isolation between sandboxes on shared hosts, so every sandbox gets the CPU, memory and I/O it was allocated

  • Building host-level observability, so we understand what every sandbox costs the host it runs on

  • Being on call for the platform you build, alongside the rest of the platform team

This role requires a high amount of ownership. You'll write the code and the design docs for the hardest changes in your area, and ship every day.

If you aren't afraid of going deep into the Linux kernel when a problem needs it, and words like eBPF, cgroups, network namespaces, nftables, conntrack, or noisy neighbor problem sound exciting to you, we want to hear from you!

What we're looking for

  • Experience building and operating systems software across a large production fleet: node agents, container or VM runtimes, schedulers, or similar

  • Strong Go, or strong Rust or C/C++ and the willingness to pick up Go quickly; our services are in Go

  • Deep Linux knowledge: processes, CPU scheduling, memory management, cgroups and namespaces, and the network stack

  • Experience making software correct under failure: crash recovery, reconciling recorded state with what is actually running, and cleanup when a process or host dies

  • For a networking focus: Linux networking for multi-tenant workloads, such as network namespaces, virtual interfaces, iptables/nftables and egress control

  • A performance mindset: you've shaved milliseconds off hot paths, profiled production systems under load, and treat p99 as a number you own

  • Excited to work in person from San Francisco

  • Comfortable with our code and infrastructure being public

We expect this experience will often come from around five or more years of relevant work, but the depth of what you've built matters more than a specific number.

  • Experience with VM or container runtimes such as Firecracker, KVM, gVisor or runc, including memory management and snapshot and restore

  • Kernel tracing and eBPF tooling

  • OS-level hardening, such as seccomp and Linux security modules

  • Running workloads on Kubernetes, which our fleet runs on

  • Contributions to the Linux kernel, Firecracker, CNCF or similar open source projects

Why this role, why now

E2B is the sandbox runtime behind Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Hugging Face, and a long list of AI labs and enterprise agent teams. We're a Series A company with over $37M raised, 8-figure revenue, and more than a billion sandboxes started. Almost all of that came from word of mouth. We have no content program, no real online presence, and a community that grew on its own while we built the product.

That's the opportunity. The developers using E2B already talk about it; nobody at the company has ever been responsible for making that visible and repeatable. You'll be the first. Founders aren't the public face of this company, so the people who own community and developer relations here own the voice, not a slice of it.

You'll join before our next funding round, with equity priced accordingly.

What you'll own

  • The event portfolio, from day one. Workshops, hackathons, technical dinners, meetups, conference presence. The events are currently run by the executive team so you will take it over in your first month and decide what stays, what goes, and what's new.

  • The ecosystem. Integrations and co-launches with agent frameworks, model providers, and infrastructure partners where E2B's users already are. Every integration is a launch with someone else's audience.

  • The community. Discord, GitHub, forums, and a creator/ambassador program that pays the users already writing and building about E2B to keep doing it publicly.

  • A budget. You propose it, you own it. We'll fund what works, and we're not shy about spending.

  • The function. You're the first person in it and we expect you to grow it as E2B grows.

What's already in place

Growth engineering builds the instrumentation and attribution, so you'll be able to see how your programs do. A customer base that includes the companies most developers in this space want to learn from.

First 90 days

Take over events and cut or reshape anything that isn't earning its place. Ship two or three framework or model-provider integrations with joint announcements. Stand up the ambassador program with the first ten people. Give us a point of view on where E2B's community actually lives and what it wants from us.

Reach and ecosystem first: integrations shipped and launched with partners, share of voice in the agent-infrastructure community, growth in community-sourced signups. Your job will be:
1. Owning technical support threads from developers and enterprise customers, from first reply to resolution
2. Debugging issues across our SDKs (Python, JS/TS), CLI, API and the platform underneath, using logs, traces and metrics and reading our source code
3. Reproducing problems against live E2B and turning them into bug reports engineering can act on
4. Handling account operations: limits, beta access, billing and usage questions
5. Fixing the docs when a customer got stuck on something they should have been able to do alone
6. Building the support tooling itself (skills, knowledge and automations for our AI agents) so the team handles more without growing at the same rate
7. Bringing what customers ask for back to product and engineering

• You follow what is happening in AI because you are curious, not because someone asked: new models, agent frameworks, coding agents
• You are comfortable when things change under you. Our product, processes and tools get rebuilt often, and you help rebuild them
• You already use AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar) in your work and want to push how far they go
• You own a problem until it is resolved, and you ask for help early when you are stuck

• Contributions to technical docs or open source
• Czech or Slovak (not required, all customer communication is in English)

Our customers are engineering teams building AI agents, and when they write to support the question is technical: a sandbox that did not resume, a template build that fails, a network rule that blocks the wrong traffic, an invoice that does not match usage. You answer with evidence, not a script.

You will join a small support team that runs much of its work through its own AI agent harness. Agents read threads, pull logs and traces, and draft replies. You decide what is true, what goes out, and what has to change so the same question does not come back. Based in Europe, you own the queue during European hours and hand off to the US.

Your job will be:
1. Owning technical support threads from developers and enterprise customers, from first reply to resolution
2. Debugging issues across our SDKs (Python, JS/TS), CLI, API and the platform underneath, using logs, traces and metrics and reading our source code
3. Reproducing problems against live E2B and turning them into bug reports engineering can act on
4. Handling account operations: limits, beta access, billing and usage questions
5. Fixing the docs when a customer got stuck on something they should have been able to do alone
6. Building the support tooling itself (skills, knowledge and automations for our AI agents) so the team handles more without growing at the same rate

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the Role

As E2B’s first engineer responsible for Trust & Safety, you’ll own and develop systems that protect our platform and customers from fraud and abuse. Your work will span payment fraud, account abuse, and misuse of compute resources, performing investigations and building detections using automation to respond.

You’ll have room to shape how we approach trust and safety as the platform grows. This is a hands-on role that combines data analysis, security investigations, and engineering. You’ll turn investigation findings into stronger detections, tools, and response processes while adapting to new patterns of abuse.

Responsibilities include:

  • Build and improve detections for payment fraud, account abuse, and misuse of free credits.

  • Investigate third-party abuse reports, evaluate the evidence, and take appropriate action.

  • Analyze logs, query data, and connect activity across systems to understand patterns of abuse.

  • Build tools and automation that help us detect, investigate, and mitigate abuse more effectively.

  • Shape our trust and safety policies and response processes, balancing effective enforcement with the needs of legitimate customers.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience in trust and safety, abuse prevention, or risk with a security focus, including hands-on investigation and mitigation.

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to work with logs, query data, and reason through ambiguous activity.

  • The engineering ability to turn investigations into practical detections, tools, and automation. We use Go, but prior Go experience isn’t required.

  • An understanding of malicious traffic and attacks, with the judgment to evaluate abuse reports and decide how to respond.

  • Experience owning problems from investigation through implementation, with the independence to build an approach as well as operate it.

Why this role, why now

Close to 3 billion sandboxes have started on E2B, and almost 200,000 teams build on us. Almost all of it came from word of mouth. Our brand assets were made with agencies, and nobody in-house owns them.

You'll be the first brand hire and the owner of how E2B looks and feels everywhere a developer meets us.

What you'll own

  • The brand identity. Logo, type, color, illustration, motion and the rules that hold them together. You decide what stays, what changes and when.

  • The website and docs. The look of e2b.dev the docs and the dashboard's marketing surfaces, built with our engineers.

  • Launch creative. Every product launch ships with visuals you directed or made: launch pages, video, social, diagrams.

  • Events and physical brand. Booths, swag, stage visuals and the office. If a developer can touch it, it's yours.

  • A brand system others can use. AI powered templates and components so marketing, sales and engineering ship on-brand work without waiting for you.

What's already in place

  • A product developers already love, and customers whose names open doors.

  • Strong brand awareness in the developer community.

  • A logo, symbol and core colors made with agencies, published at e2b.dev/brand. They're your starting point, and you decide where they go next.

First 45 days

  1. Audit every surface where E2B shows up, and write a short point of view on what the brand should be.

  2. Ship a first version of the brand system: core identity, a component set for the website, and templates for decks and social.

  3. Lead the creative for one launch end to end with product marketing.

How we'll judge year one

  • A developer recognizes E2B at a glance, without seeing the logo.

  • The website, docs, launches and events look like one company.

  • Other teams ship on-brand work without you in the loop.

  • Launch creative is good enough that people share it for its own sake.

  • The freelancers and studios you direct produce work at your standard.

Who you are

  • 8+ years in brand design, with at least 3 leading creative work in-house at a product company or at an agency.

  • You may be an associate creative director or design lead today. You've run the work, and you're ready to own the whole brand and be the one who decides, without giving up the craft to manage a team.

  • You've built or rebuilt a brand system that other people used without you in the room.

  • You can direct motion, 3D, illustration and web, and you know when to bring in a specialist.

  • You're curious about developer tools and can make infrastructure look clear instead of abstract.

  • You work well with writers, engineers and founders, and you hold your opinions loosely when someone has a better argument.

Nice to have

  • Brand work for a developer tool, cloud or AI company.

  • Experience taking a consumer-grade brand standard into a technical product.

  • Front-end skills or close work with engineers on a design system.

  • Event and physical brand design.

  • A network of freelancers and studios you can call on day one.

 - Event and physical brand design.

 - A network of freelancers and studios you can call on day one.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 9-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.

About the role

E2B has started billions of Firecracker sandboxes across regions on Google Cloud, AWS and Azure, for customers whose products stop when our sandboxes do. Reliability here is an engineering problem: the fixes for our hardest incidents land in code, not in configuration.

Your job will be to build the reliability of the platform: defining what healthy means, building the observability and automation that keep it there, and making new capabilities work reliably in production. You'll work closely with our infrastructure and systems engineers, who build the platform, and with our sandbox team in Prague.

Responsibilities include:

  • Defining SLOs and error budgets for the platform's core paths, such as sandbox start, resume and connect, and making them part of how we alert, release and prioritize

  • Building the observability and alerting that tells us the platform is healthy before customers do

  • Taking new platform capabilities from first release to working reliably in production

  • Building the automation that removes operational work, from release checks to routine fleet operations

  • Building the security and trust layers the platform's reliability depends on, such as service-to-service mutual TLS

  • Making our private cloud and enterprise deployments as reliable as our own regions

  • Running incident response, and improving how we handle incidents so a class of failure does not come back

  • Being on call, and helping shape the rotation for the rest of the platform team

This role requires a high amount of ownership. You'll write the code and the design docs for the hardest changes in your area, and ship every day.

If words like SLOs, error budgets, eBPF, Kubernetes, multi-region, or noisy neighbor problem sound exciting rather than scary, we want to hear from you!

What we're looking for

  • Experience operating large-scale distributed systems in production across regions, and making their reliability measurable

  • Strong Go (Rust or C/C++ also welcome): you take ownership of the services you build and proactively fix issues across the codebase, including in services you didn't originally write

  • Reliability engineering: you've defined SLOs and error budgets for a production service and held the platform to them

  • Incident response: you've been on call, fixed what paged you, and written post-incident reviews that led to lasting fixes

  • Experience operating Kubernetes in production

  • Infrastructure as code and GitOps, for example Terraform and Argo CD, with deep experience on at least one of GCP, AWS or Azure; we run on all three, and you don't need to know them all

  • Solid Linux and networking fundamentals: enough to debug a host under load and reason about DNS, TCP and L4/L7 load balancing

  • Operating relational databases and caches in production, including performance diagnosis

  • Excited to work in person from San Francisco

  • Comfortable with our code and infrastructure being public

We expect this experience will often come from around five or more years of relevant work, but the depth of what you've built matters more than a specific number.

Bonus points for:

  • Running observability pipelines at scale, for example Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry

  • Kernel tracing and eBPF tooling

  • Capacity planning and cost efficiency across clouds

  • Chaos engineering or deterministic simulation testing

  • Familiarity with Firecracker, KVM or how VM workloads behave on shared hosts

    • Contributions to CNCF or similar open source projects

What it’s like to work at E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with in-person (4 days on-site, 1 day WFH) offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 9-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.
